name: tssworkflow
description: TeXstudio-style workflow for VS Code: clickable file names, standalone chapter/figure compile, project-wide labels, quick error checks, Ukrainian typography, table/environment tools, frames, change preview, hovers, heading navigator, build-log warnings, quick fixes, outline, document templates (documents, fragments, several files), Activity Bar panels (commands, chapters)

commands.title: Fix typography hints in file (see fixAllCodes)
Wrap selection in environment (pick from list)
Wrap selection in command (pick from list)
Preview selection (rendered, the focus stays in the editor)
Files in Pictures/ and tikz/ with no references
Add LTeX spelling hits to the dictionary
Show cursor line in the external viewer (SyncTeX)
Diagnose SyncTeX (is this file in the PDF?)
Frame headings and formula environments (%% ---- / % ==== lines)
Normalize file (typography, tables, line breaks, frames, blank lines) with preview
Compile this file on its own (own preamble) + open PDF
Macro gallery (rendered commands of the class)
Generate MathJax macros file (for LaTeX Workshop formula preview)
Extract tikzpicture/circuitikz at cursor to tikz/ and insert \localinput
Extract all tikzpicture/circuitikz in file (or selection) to tikz/
Re-frame headings and formulas (replace existing frames)
Project statistics (words, formulas, figures per chapter)
Changes of this chapter since a git revision (latexdiff PDF)
Make template from this document (or selection)...
Build this chapter and open PDF
Page output hooks of this chapter
Rename chapter (folder, file, lists, paths, references)
Make snapshot of the project sources
Normalize all files of the project (with snapshot)
Terms: used before defined, defined but not in the index
Build only chosen parts (\part) of the main file
Format tblr / longtblr / talltblr (options and cells)
Formulas of the project (rendered, with search)
Mark / unmark the formula under the cursor as key (%! key)
Draft of the chapter summary from key formulas
Save PDF copy with a date
Check before print (fonts, picture resolution, log, TODO)
Hyphenation of words that stick into the margin (from the log)
Figures and tables far from their first reference
Reviewer notes from a PDF to TODO comments
Word count of the project (by chapter and file)

editor/title.when: (resourceLangId == latex || resourceLangId == tex || resourceExtname == .tikz) && !tssworkflow.building && resourceExtname != .cls && resourceExtname != .sty && resourceExtname != .clo && resourceExtname != .def && resourceExtname != .cfg

tssworkflow.driver.description: Driver .tex file in the workspace root

tssworkflow.pdfBeside.description: Open the PDF in a side-by-side editor group

tssworkflow.jobname.description: Output name (jobname) for standalone builds. Empty = name of the open file. "main" makes SyncTeX work with % !TeX root = ../main.tex

tssworkflow.compilePasses.main.description: How many times the whole document (Shift+F5, the main file, tssworkflow.mainFile) is run through the engine. Exactly N runs of plain lualatex in a row; biber (when <job>.bcf exists) or bibtex (when the .aux asks for a database) runs between the first and the second run. The status bar shows the exact run number, e.g. 2/4. 0: latexmk decides how many runs are needed (the total is then the number of runs of the previous build).

tssworkflow.compilePasses.separate.description: The same for a file built on its own (a document with its own \documentclass, button ▷ Separate): exactly N runs of the engine of tssworkflow.compileCurrent.engine in the folder of the build, with biber / bibtex after the first run. 0: latexmk decides.

tssworkflow.compilePasses.chapter.description: The same for a chapter or a figure (button ▷ Chapter / Figure, F5, Auto): exactly N runs of plain lualatex through the driver (tssworkflow.driver); biber / makeindex are not run, references come from the existing <jobname>.aux. 0: latexmk decides.

tssworkflow.openPdf.main.description: Open the PDF when the build of the whole document (Shift+F5, the main file) has finished. Off: the build runs and the PDF is only rewritten.

tssworkflow.openPdf.separate.description: Open the PDF when the build of a file with its own \documentclass (Ctrl+F5) has finished. Off: the build runs and the PDF is only rewritten.

tssworkflow.openPdf.chapter.description: Open the PDF when the build of a chapter or a figure (F5) has finished. Off: the build runs and the PDF is only rewritten.

tssworkflow.biber.description: biber executable run between the first and the second LaTeX run of the whole document and of a separate file, when <job>.bcf exists (tssworkflow.compilePasses.main / .separate > 1).

tssworkflow.bibtex.description: bibtex executable run between the first and the second LaTeX run of the whole document and of a separate file, when there is no <job>.bcf but <job>.aux contains \bibdata (tssworkflow.compilePasses.main / .separate > 1).

tssworkflow.singlePass.description: Superseded by tssworkflow.compilePasses.chapter (default 1: one run of plain lualatex). Kept for old settings: it only matters when singlePass = false and passes > 0, and only while compilePasses.chapter is not set.

tssworkflow.buildSeconds.description: Show the seconds counter next to the running build in the status bar. false: the text only changes when the pass number changes (nothing is redrawn every second, as in LaTeX Workshop); use it if the spinner still looks jerky

tssworkflow.passes.description: Superseded by tssworkflow.compilePasses.chapter. Kept for old settings: with singlePass = false, N (1-9) is the number of runs of a chapter / figure build, while compilePasses.chapter is not set. 0 no longer means latexmk: set compilePasses.chapter = 0 for that.

tssworkflow.showPasses.description: Show the number of the LaTeX run in the status bar. With a fixed number of runs (tssworkflow.compilePasses.*) it is exact, e.g. 2/4; in latexmk builds (compilePasses = 0) it is detected from changes of <job>.log, and the total is the number of runs of the previous build of the same file (unknown on the first one). For one run (a chapter) the 1/1 is shown only if this is on.

tssworkflow.lualatex.description: lualatex executable used for the builds with a fixed number of runs (tssworkflow.compilePasses.*)

tssworkflow.forceRebuild.description: Pass -g to latexmk so a build sharing the jobname with the full document is always redone

tssworkflow.wrapWidth.description: Line width for the "Wrap paragraph" command and for Normalize file with normalizeLineBreaks = wrap

tssworkflow.diagnostics.description: Quick error checks (missing backslash, unpaired environments, blank line in formula, missing files) and project label checks on save

tssworkflow.compileOnSave.description: Compile the current chapter or figure after saving (root files are skipped). Also toggled from the status bar

tssworkflow.previewChanges.description: Show a side-by-side preview (Apply / Cancel) before frames and "Normalize file" change the text

tssworkflow.typographyOnSave.description: Apply Ukrainian typography (~, ~---, «») to the whole .tex file on every save

tssworkflow.unusedLabels.description: How to mark labels that no \ref points to

tssworkflow.labelPrefixes.description: Required label prefix by environment, e.g. {"equation": "eq:", "figure": "pic:"}. Use an empty object to disable

tssworkflow.logWarnings.description: After a build, show Overfull \hbox and undefined references from the .log in Problems. false: with pplatex / texlogsieve only errors stay; with builtin nothing from the log

tssworkflow.preflight.minDpi.markdownDescription: Check before print: a raster picture printed below this resolution (ppi, as placed on the page, read with `pdfimages -list`) is reported. 300 is the usual demand of a printing house; 150 is enough for a PDF read on screen.

tssworkflow.preflight.requireCmyk.markdownDescription: Check before print: report RGB pictures as a problem (the printing house wants CMYK). Off: they are only counted.

tssworkflow.floatMaxPages.markdownDescription: Figures and tables far from their first reference (also a part of Check before print): how many pages after the page of the first `\ref` a float may stand. 0: only on the same page; 1: the same or the next one.

tssworkflow.frameRules.description: Rule line of the frames. Keys: "headings" (all sectioning commands), "formulas" (all formula environments), or a single command / environment name (chapter, section, subsection, subsubsection, paragraph, subparagraph, equation, align, gather, multline, eqnarray, flalign, alignat, displaymath). Value: a comment line of 8+ identical characters - = * # _ ~ . , or "" to switch framing off for that key. Example: {"headings": "%% ----------------------", "section": "%%% ======================", "equation": ""}. Empty object = defaults (%% + 56 dashes for headings, % + 56 "=" for formulas). Key "environments" sets the look of the extra environments from frameEnvironments.

tssworkflow.frameBlankLines.description: Add a blank line above and below a framed heading

enumDescriptions: Ukrainian messages and reports (as before)

English messages and reports where a translation exists (build and its status bar, the log of LaTeX and Problems, wrap in command and environment, Doctor, table editor, macro gallery, formula overview, selection preview, tblr and tikz formatting, citations and project settings, state of the extension, normalize, framing, new chapter, DOI to BibTeX, latexdiff, project statistics, typography hints and macros, labels and files: rename of labels and files, packages, tables, .bib, equations, the project reports, snapshots, rename and move of chapters, replace in project, notation, terms); the rest stays Ukrainian for now
English unless the display language of VS Code is Ukrainian
tssworkflow.language.description: Language of the messages, prompts and reports of the extension. Partly translated: see the changelog for what is covered.

tssworkflow.mainFile.description: Root file of the whole document (in the workspace root), built by Shift+F5 and when a root file is open

tssworkflow.normalizeFrames.description: Normalize file: frame headings and formula environments (see tssworkflow.frameRules)

tssworkflow.normalizeBlankLines.description: Normalize file: one blank line between paragraphs (tssworkflow.blankLinesParagraph), tssworkflow.blankLinesHeading blank lines before and after every sectioning command. Verbatim and formula environments are not touched

enumDescriptions: Do not touch line breaks
Join the lines of every paragraph into one line
Join, then break lines longer than tssworkflow.wrapWidth
tssworkflow.normalizeLineBreaks.description: Normalize file: what to do with hard line breaks inside paragraphs. Formulas, verbatim, tikzpicture, tables and the preamble are never touched; nothing is done in .tikz files

tssworkflow.blankLinesParagraph.description: Normalize file: blank lines between paragraphs

tssworkflow.blankLinesHeading.description: Normalize file: blank lines before and after \part, \chapter, \section, \subsection, \subsubsection, \paragraph, \subparagraph (with their frame lines and \label)

enumDescriptions: Open the PDF in VS Code (beside the editor) after a build with PDF
Open the PDF through LaTeX Workshop's viewer (command latex-workshop.view); use this when LaTeX Workshop is installed: plain 'vscode' leaves an empty tab
Open the PDF in the external viewer after a build with PDF
Do not open the PDF after a build
tssworkflow.pdfViewer.description: Where the PDF opens after the buttons that compile and open the PDF

tssworkflow.externalViewerCommand.description: Program for the 'Open PDF in external viewer' button (must be in PATH or a full path), e.g. SumatraPDF, okular, open, xdg-open

tssworkflow.externalViewerArgs.description: Arguments of the external viewer. ${pdf}: the PDF, ${file}: the active .tex file, ${line}: cursor line (1-based). If ${pdf} is absent, the PDF path is appended

tssworkflow.externalSyncArgs.description: Arguments for the command 'Show cursor line in the external viewer (SyncTeX)'. Same placeholders as externalViewerArgs. Default is for SumatraPDF

tssworkflow.projectSettingsTemplate.description: Path to a JSON(C) file used as the template for 'Create .vscode/settings.json for this project' instead of the built-in one. The built-in template is generated for the project: mainFile (the only .tex of the root, else main.tex, else you are asked), jobname, macroFiles (.sty/.cls in subfolders), the style of the text, texlogsieve when the program is found, MathJax macros of LaTeX Workshop and files.exclude for build files. A custom template is used as it is.

tssworkflow.offerProjectSettings.description: When a folder with .tex files has no .vscode/settings.json, offer to create it from the template (can be silenced per folder)

tssworkflow.lwCompat.notify.description: At start, when the Auto build of this extension and the autoBuild of LaTeX Workshop are both on (two builds into the same files on every save), offer once per workspace to fix it. The command 'Check compatibility with LaTeX Workshop' works either way

enumDescriptions: Do not start a build, an automatic build or a clean of this extension while LaTeX Workshop (or a latexmk in a terminal) is building the same document: the same <job>.aux, .log, .pdf
The same, but for a build of any file under the project folder
Never check: the build starts at once (two builds at the same time spoil each other's .aux and .pdf)
tssworkflow.lwGuard.description: Block the build of this extension while LaTeX Workshop is compiling the same document. LaTeX Workshop does not announce its builds, so the list of processes is read when a build is about to start (one reading, no timer); a build with a command line that cannot be read is never blocked. A command offers to wait, to stop the LaTeX Workshop build or to start anyway; the automatic build (Auto) is skipped with a line in the status bar. Only with LaTeX Workshop installed

tssworkflow.citationChecks.description: On save, check \cite keys against the .bib files of the workspace (undefined keys, duplicates). Only .bib files inside the workspace are read

tssworkflow.unusedBibEntries.description: How to mark .bib entries that no \cite refers to (not reported if the project has \nocite{*})

tssworkflow.figureChecks.description: How to mark figure / figure* / wrapfigure / wrapstuff[type=figure] without \caption or without \label

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression, applied to the code part of each line (comments are skipped)

flags.description: Regex flags: i, m, s, u (g is always on)

files.description: Regular expression tested against the file path (with /); the rule applies only to matching files

tssworkflow.lintRules.description: Own lint rules, e.g. [{"pattern": "\\\\varepsilon_0", "message": "SI constant in a CGS text", "files": "EMConspect"}]

enumDescriptions: Errors from the latexmk output (file-line-error) plus the built-in log parser (Overfull, undefined references)
Run pplatex on <job>.log after every build and show its Errors, Warnings and BadBoxes in Problems instead
Run texlogsieve on <job>.log after every build and show its Errors, Warnings, Overfull boxes and Missing characters in Problems (project files only)
tssworkflow.logParser.description: Where the Problems entries after a build come from

tssworkflow.pplatexCommand.description: pplatex executable (ppluatex, ppdflatex or pplatex: it is the same program); must be in PATH or a full path. Used when tssworkflow.logParser = pplatex

tssworkflow.pplatexBadBoxes.description: Severity of pplatex BadBox entries (Overfull/Underfull); Overfull narrower than tssworkflow.overfullThreshold is skipped

enumDescriptions: Straight "..." and ``...'' become «...»
"...", ``...'', <<...>> and «...» become \enquote{...} (the csquotes package is needed)
Do not touch quotes
tssworkflow.quoteStyle.description: What typography (the Typography command, typographyOnSave and Normalize file) does with quotes

tssworkflow.texlogsieveCommand.description: Executable of texlogsieve (name in PATH or full path); used when tssworkflow.logParser = texlogsieve

tssworkflow.texlogsieveArgs.description: Arguments for texlogsieve. ${log} is replaced with the path to <job>.log (added at the end if missing). Check `texlogsieve --help` for options

enumDescriptions: After every build show the grouped report in the 'texlogsieve' Output channel
Show the channel only when there is something to report (it is still refreshed after every build)
Do not write the Output channel
tssworkflow.texlogsieveOutput.description: Grouped problem report (errors, warnings, missing characters, Overfull/Underfull; clickable file:line) in its own Output channel after each build (used when tssworkflow.logParser = texlogsieve)

enumDescriptions: After every build show the texlogsieve report in the 'texlogsieve' terminal tab
Show the tab only when there are errors or warnings (an already open tab is still refreshed)
Do not show the report
tssworkflow.texlogsieveTerminal.description: Print the full texlogsieve report in a separate terminal tab after each build (used when tssworkflow.logParser = texlogsieve)

tssworkflow.macros.description: Completion, hover, go-to-definition and signature help for macros and environments defined in the project's own .cls/.sty (found via \documentclass / \usepackage in main.tex) and in the open file

tssworkflow.macroFiles.description: Extra files (or globs) with macro definitions, relative to the workspace folder, e.g. ["ConspectBook.cls", "styles/*.sty"]. Normally not needed: the class and local packages are found automatically

enumDescriptions: Insert tab stops for mandatory arguments only
Insert tab stops for optional arguments too
Insert the bare command name
tssworkflow.macroSnippetArgs.description: What is inserted when a macro from the class is accepted from the completion list

tssworkflow.mathjaxMacrosFile.description: File (next to main.tex) written by 'Generate MathJax macros file'. Its name goes to latex-workshop.hover.preview.newcommand.newcommandFile

tssworkflow.mathjaxAutoUpdate.description: Regenerate the MathJax macros file when a project .cls/.sty is saved (only if the file already exists)

tssworkflow.tikzExtractEnvs.description: Environments that 'Extract tikzpicture/circuitikz to tikz/' moves into tikz/<name>.tikz (e.g. add tikzcd or axis). The name is the \label of the enclosing figure without the prefix before the colon

tssworkflow.tikzExtractInline.description: Extract tikzpicture/circuitikz to tikz/: also move inline \tikz[...]{...} and \tikz \draw ...; (not \tikzset and the like) into tikz/<n>.tikz. The ones inside a moved environment go with it. false: environments from tikzExtractEnvs only (as before 0.6.1).

tssworkflow.frameEnvironments.description: Extra environments to frame like formulas (e.g. ["SCfigure", "theorem"]). Their rule line comes from frameRules (key = the environment name, else "environments", else "formulas"). The built-in ones (equation, align, gather, multline, eqnarray, flalign, alignat, displaymath) are always framed.

tssworkflow.typographyChecks.description: Severity of the typography checks: a plain space between a number and a unit or after "рис." / "табл." / "п." (use ~), a hyphen instead of the dash, a word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters, \\vec and \\vect mixed in one file (see mixedMacros). "off" switches them off. Quick fixes are offered for the first three and for look-alike letters.

tssworkflow.mixedMacros.description: Pairs of macro names that should not be mixed within one file, e.g. [["vec", "vect"]]. The less frequent one is marked. Empty list = no check.

tssworkflow.protectedCommands.description: Names of your own commands whose arguments are code, not text. The typography checks and the typography command (Ctrl+Alt+T, normalize) do not touch them, just like \tikz{...}, \tikzset{...}, \pgfkeys{...}, which are always protected. A name takes one {...} group (after any [...] groups); 'name:2' takes two. Example: ['mytikz', 'myfig:2']. The backslash is optional. Single lines can also be excluded with % tss-ignore comments.

tssworkflow.fixAllCodes.description: Which typography hints 'fix all' corrects: the command Fix typography hints in file and the code action source.fixAll.tssworkflow (for editor.codeActionsOnSave). typo-nbsp = plain space after a number or abbreviation (becomes ~), typo-dash = hyphen instead of the dash (becomes ---), typo-mixed-script = Latin look-alikes inside Cyrillic words. Default: only typo-nbsp.

tssworkflow.todoKeywords.description: Words that mark a note in a % comment for the TSS TODO view in the Explorer. \\todo{...} commands are always listed.

tssworkflow.stats.builtinCounters.description: Project statistics: add the columns Problems and Control questions (see stats.problemEnvs, stats.questionTitle).

tssworkflow.stats.problemEnvs.description: Project statistics: environments counted as problems (each \begin{name} is one), e.g. ["problem", "exercise"].

tssworkflow.stats.questionEnvs.description: Project statistics: environments whose items are the control questions: every \item at the first level of \begin{name} is one (a nested list is not counted), anywhere in the file. Empty list: the lists inside the section whose title matches stats.questionTitle are counted instead.

tssworkflow.stats.exclude.description: Project statistics: files and folders that are left out of the table and of the total, as in .gitignore: a name without / matches at any depth (a folder: everything inside; a file: with or without .tex), a path with / (or / in front) is counted from the project root; * ** ? work; a closing / means a folder only. E.g. ["Preface", "Appendix/Tests/", "**/draft*.tex"].

tssworkflow.stats.questionTitle.markdownDescription: Project statistics, only when `stats.questionEnvs` is empty: regular expression (case-insensitive, Unicode) for the title of the control-questions section; the items of the lists inside it (until the next heading of the same or a higher level) are counted. Empty: `Контрольні запитання`, `Контрольні питання`, `Питання для самоперевірки`, `Запитання до розділу`, `Review questions`.

tssworkflow.statsCounters.description: Extra counters of the statistics command: name -> regular expression, e.g. {"Задачі": "\\\\begin\\{problem\\}"}. Counted in the text without comments.

tssworkflow.auxFile.description: Path (relative to the project folder) of the .aux file used for the label number and page in hovers. Empty = <jobname>.aux, then build/<jobname>.aux.

enumDescriptions: Thumbnail by a file: URI (any size up to imagePreviewMaxMB)
Thumbnail embedded as base64 (only files up to 64 KB; larger ones are not drawn by VS Code)
No thumbnail, only the 'Open image' link
tssworkflow.imagePreviewMode.description: How the hover on \includegraphics shows the picture

tssworkflow.imagePreviewMaxMB.description: Largest picture (MB) the hover on \includegraphics draws as a thumbnail; a larger file gets a short message and the 'Open image' link instead. 0: never draw thumbnails

tssworkflow.figureTemplate.description: Lines inserted when a picture is dropped or pasted into a .tex file. Placeholders: ${name} (file name without extension), ${width}, ${label}, ${caption} (the cursor stops here). Inside an existing figure only \includegraphics is inserted

tssworkflow.newTikzTemplate.description: Content of a .tikz file created by the Quick Fix on a \localinput without a file. Placeholder: ${name}

tssworkflow.chapterTemplate.description: Content of <name>/<name>.tex created by the command New chapter. Placeholders: ${name}, ${title}, ${root} (path to the main file, ../main.tex)

tssworkflow.chapterIncludeMacro.description: Macro whose line `\includechapter{name}` the command New chapter adds to the main file (after the last such line)

tssworkflow.staleRefsIndicator.description: Show «refs застарілі» in the status bar when a source file was saved after the last whole-document build (references and table of contents of chapter builds come from <jobname>.aux)

tssworkflow.latexdiffArgs.description: Arguments of latexdiff before the two file names (old, new)

tssworkflow.templatesDir.description: Folder with your document templates (.tex, .tikz) for 'New from template'. Empty: the extension's own storage folder (see 'Open user templates folder'). A leading ~ is the home folder

tssworkflow.projectTemplatesDir.description: Folder with project templates, relative to the workspace folder (or absolute). Project templates are listed first in 'New from template'. Empty: no project templates

tssworkflow.templateAuthor.description: Value of ${author} in templates (also available: ${date}, ${year}, ${time}, ${title} - asked when the template uses it, ${cursor} - where the caret stops)

tssworkflow.newFromTemplateInWorkspace.description: New from template: when no folder was clicked, create the file in the folder VS Code is open in (asks only for the name; no Save As dialog). false: an untitled document, as before 0.4.4. With no folder open the document is untitled anyway.

tssworkflow.chapterTemplateName.description: Name of a template (see 'New from template') whose text becomes the content of a chapter made by 'New chapter'. Placeholders: ${name}, ${title}, ${root}, ${date}, ${year}, ${time}, ${author}, ${cursor}. Empty: the setting chapterTemplate is used

enumDescriptions: Ukrainian labels
English labels (the titles of the commands)
As the setting tssworkflow.language says (with tssworkflow.language = auto: English unless VS Code is Ukrainian)
tssworkflow.panelLanguage.description: Language of the labels in the Activity Bar panel. The default follows tssworkflow.language, which is Ukrainian by default, so nothing changes until that one is set.

tssworkflow.statusBarMain.description: Show the status bar button 'Main' that builds the whole document and opens the PDF

tssworkflow.chapterListMacros.description: Macros that include several chapters as a comma list, e.g. \multiinclude{A, B, C}[]. The 'Розділи' panel reads the chapters from them (together with chapterIncludeMacro) and groups them by \part. Empty list: only chapterIncludeMacro. 'New chapter' adds the new chapter to the end of such a list when the main file has no chapterIncludeMacro lines

tssworkflow.checkEnvironmentOnStart.description: Once, at the start of a project with .tex files, warn if latexmk or lualatex is not found in PATH and offer to run 'Check environment'.

tssworkflow.snapshotsKeep.description: How many project snapshots to keep (the oldest are deleted). Snapshots are taken before renaming a chapter, Replace in project, Normalize project and notation unify, and by Make snapshot.

tssworkflow.citeCompletion.description: Completion of keys inside \cite{...} from the .bib files of the project (author, year, title are shown and searchable), and a hover with the entry over a key.

tssworkflow.termMacros.description: Macros whose argument is a term being defined (\emph{...}). "Terms" takes the first such place in the order of the book as the definition and reports the same words used in the text before it.

tssworkflow.termsIgnore.description: Words and phrases that "Terms" skips (a \emph used for emphasis, not for a definition).

tssworkflow.termsForms.description: Groups of forms of one word that "Terms" treats as the same word when the vowel of the stem changes: [["потік", "потоку", "потоком"]]. Single words only; case does not matter.

tssworkflow.notationGroups.description: Groups of notations for "Notation consistency". Empty = the built-in groups (\varepsilon/\epsilon, \varphi/\phi, \leqslant/\leq/\le, \geqslant/\geq/\ge, \mathrm{d}/\mathrm d, units in \mathrm/\text).

pattern.description: JavaScript regex; one capture group may carry the payload

make.description: What this variant looks like when written (with $1 for the payload)

tssworkflow.tblr.maxWidth.description: Format tblr: a table whose rows fit in this width gets a grid (cells aligned at &); otherwise a long row is written one cell per line.

tssworkflow.tikzFormat.minLength.description: Format inline \tikz{...}: only a \tikz[...]{...} written on one line and at least this many characters long is laid out one statement per line (shorter ones, like a small icon in the text, stay as they are; 0 = all). Code already in several lines is never touched.

tssworkflow.tblr.sortOptions.description: Format tblr: order the keys colspec, rowhead/rowfoot, hline/vline, column, row, cell, the rest (the order inside a group is kept, a later key still overrides an earlier one). Off: keep the original order.

tssworkflow.tblr.formatOnSave.description: Format all tblr / longtblr / talltblr tables of a .tex file when it is saved (no preview; one Ctrl+Z undoes it).

tssworkflow.beamer.autoRenumber.description: Renumber the "% === Слайд N ===" banners of a beamer file when it is saved (no preview; one Ctrl+Z undoes it).

tssworkflow.beamer.skipTitleFrame.description: Renumber Beamer Slides: do not number the frame with \titlepage / \maketitle; the first following frame is slide 1.

tssworkflow.excludeFolders.markdownDescription: More folders that are not part of the project: labels, the chapters panel, the statistics, the search of .bib/.sty/pictures and the renames do not look into them. A plain name (`old`) means `**/old/**`; a value with `/` or `*` is a glob. `build`, `.archive`, `node_modules` and `.git` are always excluded.

tssworkflow.fileMacros.markdownDescription: Table **macro → folder** for Ctrl+click, name completion and the "file not found" check. The folder is relative to the current file (for `\\input` and `\\include` the project root is tried first, see `tssworkflow.inputRoot`). `"."` is the same folder. An empty string or `null` switches a macro off. Add your own: `{"\\\\myfig": "figs"}`. Extensions: `.tikz`, `.tex` (pictures for `\\includegraphics`).

tssworkflow.inputRoot.markdownDescription: How `\\input` and `\\include` paths are read. `workspace`: from the project root, because the document and `alone.tex` are built there (a path relative to the chapter folder is reported with a Quick Fix); `file`: relative to the current file; `off`: no check of the root.

tssworkflow.rootRelativeMacros.markdownDescription: Macros whose paths are relative to the build folder (the project root), see `tssworkflow.inputRoot`.

tssworkflow.tikzIncludeMacro.markdownDescription: What `Extract tikzpicture to tikz/` writes in place of the picture. `auto`: `\\localinput{name}` if the project defines `\\localinput` in a `.cls`/`.sty`/`.tex`, otherwise `\\input{<chapter>/tikz/name}`.

tssworkflow.updateRefsOnRename.markdownDescription: After a file or folder (picture, `.tikz`, `.tex`) is renamed or moved in the Explorer: update the `\\includegraphics`, `\\localinput`, `\\input` ... that point to it. `ask`: show the number of references first.

tssworkflow.tlmgrCommand.markdownDescription: Command prefix of the Quick Fix for a missing package, e.g. `sudo tlmgr install` or `tlmgr --usermode install`.

tssworkflow.wordCount.description: Status bar: number of words of the current file (the selection in brackets).

tssworkflow.labels.eqPrefixes.markdownDescription: Label prefixes (`eq:...`) for which the Labels panel inserts `\\eqref{}`; for others `\\ref{}`.

tssworkflow.bib.sortBy.description: Format .bib: sort the entries (none keeps the order).

tssworkflow.bib.sortFields.description: Format .bib: put the fields in the usual order (author, title, journal, volume, pages, year, doi ...).

tssworkflow.tblr.headerColor.description: Table from CSV / XLSX: background colour of the header row.

tssworkflow.tblr.oddRowColor.description: Table from CSV / XLSX: colour of odd rows.

tssworkflow.tblr.csvFloat.description: Table from CSV / XLSX: wrap in table with \caption and \label (false: only tblr).

tssworkflow.pdfCopyDir.description: Save PDF copy with a date: folder (relative to the project root).

tssworkflow.pdfCopyTime.description: Save PDF copy: add the time (HHMM) after the date.

enumDescriptions: Build in the folder of the file: the PDF and the aux files are written next to it.
Build in the workspace folder (like the whole document): paths in the file are relative to it.
tssworkflow.compileCurrent.workDir.description: Compile this file on its own: where latexmk runs and writes its files.

tssworkflow.compileCurrent.engine.description: Compile this file on its own: the TeX engine (the other builds of the extension use lualatex).

enumDescriptions: Buttons above the selected text: Bold, Italic, Underline and a Format menu. They appear a moment after the selection stops changing and push the lines below down while shown.
Only the light bulb (Ctrl+.) on a selection, the text does not move.
Buttons and the light bulb.
Nothing is shown; the command Format selection stays in the palette.
tssworkflow.wrapCmd.selectionHint.description: What is offered when text is selected in a .tex file: formatting it as bold, italic, underline, ...

enumDescriptions: With nothing selected the panel shows the paragraph around the caret.
With nothing selected the panel shows nothing.
tssworkflow.selectionPreview.emptySelect.description: Preview selection: what is shown when no text is selected.

tssworkflow.tableEditor.prefetch.description: Table editor: when a file with tables is shown, look for the colours and macros of the project in the background, so that the grid opens at once (the search is repeated at most every 5 minutes and after a file with colour definitions is saved).

enumDescriptions: The file stays where it is.
A click or a move to another row in the grid scrolls the file to that row of the table (the focus stays in the grid).
Like reveal, and the table and the active row are highlighted in the file.
Like highlight, and the text caret is put at the start of the active row.
tssworkflow.tableEditor.followEditor.description: Table editor: how the file follows the grid.

tssworkflow.tableEditor.codeLens.description: Show "Edit table" above tblr / longtblr / tabular ... environments.

tssworkflow.tableEditor.alignAfterEdit.description: Table editor: a table whose cells were aligned (& under & ) stays aligned after an edit; a tblr table in the "Format tblr" style is formatted again.

tssworkflow.doctorOnStartup.description: When a project is opened, warn once if latexmk or lualatex is not in PATH (offers Doctor and "do not remind").

tssworkflow.wrapEnv.extra.markdownDescription: Own entries of the list in `Wrap selection in environment` (`Ctrl+Alt+W`). Each is an environment name, optionally with arguments: `"minipage{0.5\\linewidth}"`, `"figure[htbp]"`, `"tcolorbox"`. `{}` and `[]` are where the caret stops after wrapping.

tssworkflow.wrapEnv.indent.description: Wrap selection in environment: indent the wrapped lines one step (not in verbatim, lstlisting, minted).

tssworkflow.wrapEnv.label.markdownDescription: Wrap selection in environment: add `\label{prefix}` when the environment has a prefix in `tssworkflow.labelPrefixes` (floats: after the wrapped text, other environments: right after `\begin`). Not added when the wrapped text already has a `\label`.

tssworkflow.wrapCmd.extra.markdownDescription: Own entries of the list in `Wrap selection in command` (`Ctrl+Alt+K`). Each is a command name, optionally with the arguments that stand before the wrapped one: `"vect"`, `"textcolor{red}"`, `"href{https://example.org}"`.

tssworkflow.selectionPreview.steps.description: Preview selection: show a derivation (align, gather, aligned in equation) with the changes between neighbouring rows coloured and the buttons ◀ ▶ to go through the rows one by one.

enumDescriptions: Copy the formula as MathML (Word, PowerPoint, LibreOffice take it as an equation).
Copy the TeX code of the formula.
Ask each time.
tssworkflow.copyFormula.format.description: Copy formula: what goes into the clipboard.

target.description: current: the file of the editor (chapter, figure or standalone document); main: the whole document (tssworkflow.mainFile)

openPdf.description: Open the PDF after a successful build (false: build only)
